name: Run kube-bench against node and master
objective: CKS › Cluster Setup + System Hardening (10% + 15%). Drill the kube-bench workflow harder than the exam: run it as a Job against node AND master, read [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN], then remediate every recurring finding — manifest & PKI file modes, the kubelet read-only port, the apiserver NodeRestriction plugin — plus a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Audit a worker node with kube-bench
questions.teach:
**kube-bench** audits a node against the **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark**, printing `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, or `[WARN]` per numbered control. Because it inspects the host's real files, run it **on the node** — as a Job with `hostPID: true` and hostPath mounts — and read findings from the pod logs.

**Gotcha:** a plain pod without `hostPID` and host mounts reads the container's filesystem, not the host, giving bogus results.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench` using image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest` with args `["run","--targets","node"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, and hostPath mounts for `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/etc/kubernetes`, and `/etc/systemd`. Wait for it to complete.

Target: Job `kube-bench` in `cks-bench` has a completed pod whose logs contain at least one of `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, `[WARN]`.
questions.hint: Apply a Job with `restartPolicy: Never`, `hostPID: true`, image `aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","node"]`, and hostPath volumes for the three host paths. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: { name: kube-bench, namespace: cks-bench }
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      restartPolicy: Never
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run","--targets","node"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes, mountPath: /etc/kubernetes, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd, mountPath: /etc/systemd, readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes, hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd, hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
YAML
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]' | head

verification.description: Job kube-bench completed with hostPID and host mounts; logs contain CIS [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WARN]

questions.eli5:
Imagine your cluster node is a house, and there's an official safety checklist (the **CIS Benchmark**) that says things like "the front-door lock must be this strong" and "the gas valve must be off." **kube-bench** is a building inspector who walks the house with that checklist and, for each item, shouts one of three things:

- **`[PASS]`** — "This is fine."
- **`[FAIL]`** — "This is wrong, fix it."
- **`[WARN]`** — "I can't check this one myself — you go look."

Here's the catch: the inspector has to walk the *real* house, not a cardboard photo of it. So you can't just send him into a sealed box (a plain pod that only sees its own little container filesystem). You give him **keys to the real rooms** — `hostPID: true` so he sees the node's real processes, and **hostPath mounts** so he reads the node's real files under `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/etc/kubernetes`, and `/etc/systemd`. You run him as a short one-time visit (a **Job**), and when he's done you read his report from the pod **logs**.

**Watch out for:**

- **No host keys = garbage report.** A plain pod without `hostPID` and the hostPath mounts inspects the *container's* files, not the node's, so every finding is bogus.
- **It's a Job, so use `restartPolicy: Never`** — it runs once and completes; it isn't a long-running service.
- **Read the report from the logs**: `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench`. Grep for `[PASS]`, `[FAIL]`, `[WARN]`.
- **`--targets node`** only covers worker/kubelet checks (CIS section 4) — not the control plane (that's the next step).
questions.deepDive:
## Running kube-bench against a node — full rundown

### Mental model
`kube-bench` is Aqua Security's implementation of the **CIS Kubernetes Benchmark**. It inspects the files, processes, and flags on a node and prints a numbered result line per control. Because the checks read the **host's** real state (file modes, running process args, config files), the scanner must see the host — not a container sandbox. You achieve that with `hostPID: true` and `hostPath` mounts. Run it as a one-shot **Job** and read findings from the pod logs.

### Result markers
| Marker | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `[PASS]` | Control is satisfied | Nothing |
| `[FAIL]` | Control is violated | Remediate (the output prints a fix) |
| `[WARN]` | Automated check impossible / manual review | Verify manually; often a flag kube-bench can't read |
| `[INFO]` | Informational | Context only |

Each line is prefixed with a CIS **control number** (e.g. `4.1.1`, `1.1.11`). The scanner also prints a `== Remediations ==` section and a `== Summary ==` with counts.

### CIS section → `--targets`
| `--targets` | CIS section | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `node` | 4.x | kubelet config/service, proxy, worker file perms |
| `master` | 1.x | apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, etcd, PKI |
| `etcd` | 2.x | etcd data dir / flags |
| `controlplane` | 3.x | authn/authz, logging policies |
| `policies` | 5.x | RBAC, Pod Security, network policies (mostly `[WARN]`) |

`--targets node` scans only section 4 — the worker/kubelet surface.

### The Job manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kube-bench
  namespace: cks-bench
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true                 # see the node's real process tree
      restartPolicy: Never          # one-shot; Jobs can't use Always
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run","--targets","node"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes,  mountPath: /etc/kubernetes,  readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd,     mountPath: /etc/systemd,     readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes,  hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd,     hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
```

### Why each mount matters
| Host path | Why kube-bench needs it |
|---|---|
| `/var/lib/kubelet` | kubelet `config.yaml` perms + settings (section 4) |
| `/etc/kubernetes` | manifests, PKI, kubeconfig files (section 1 perms) |
| `/etc/systemd` | kubelet service unit / drop-ins |

### Run and read
```bash
kubectl apply -f kube-bench-job.yaml
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]' | head
# just the failures:
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep '\[FAIL\]'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **No `hostPID` + no host mounts → bogus results.** The scanner reads the container's filesystem/process tree, not the node's. The whole report is meaningless.
- **`restartPolicy` must be `Never` (or `OnFailure`).** `Always` is invalid for a Job and `kubectl apply` rejects it.
- **It's a one-shot.** Don't expect a running pod — `wait --for=condition=complete`, then read logs. Deleting the Job deletes the pod and its logs.
- **`[WARN]` is not `[PASS]`.** A warn usually means kube-bench couldn't read a flag; verify it manually before claiming compliance.
- **`--targets node` won't show section 1 (master) findings** — those files don't exist on a worker. Use `--targets master` on the control plane (next step).
- **`latest` tag drift**: pin a benchmark version with `--benchmark cis-1.x` on the exam if results look off for your cluster version.

### Quick reference
```bash
# apply + wait + read
kubectl -n cks-bench apply -f kube-bench-job.yaml
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\]'
```
Essentials: `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, hostPath mounts for `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/etc/kubernetes`, `/etc/systemd`, args `["run","--targets","node"]`.

questions.title: Audit the control plane (--targets master)
questions.teach:
`--targets node` only covers the kubelet/worker checks (CIS section 4). The control-plane checks (apiserver, scheduler, etcd — CIS section 1) live under `--targets master` and only appear when kube-bench runs **on a control-plane node** where those files exist.

**Gotcha:** a master-targets Job landing on a worker finds no control-plane files — pin it to the control-plane node with a nodeSelector + toleration.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-bench`, create a Job named `kube-bench-master` (`aquasec/kube-bench:latest`, args `["run","--targets","master"]`, `hostPID: true`, `restartPolicy: Never`, same three hostPath mounts) that is pinned to the control-plane node so it can read `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`. Wait for completion.

Target: Job `kube-bench-master` completed on the control-plane node; its logs contain a CIS **1.x** master finding (e.g. `[PASS] 1.` or `[FAIL] 1.`).
questions.hint: Add `nodeSelector: { node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: "" }` and a control-plane toleration so it lands on `$CP`. Use args `["run","--targets","master"]`. Then `kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench-master | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\] 1\.'`.

verification.description: Job kube-bench-master ran on the control plane and logged CIS section 1.x (master) findings

questions.eli5:
In the last step the inspector checked the *worker's* rooms. But a cluster has a special, more important building: the **control plane** — the brain room with the apiserver, scheduler, and etcd. That building has its own, stricter checklist (**CIS section 1**), and its paperwork lives in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests` on the control-plane node.

Here's the problem: the inspector can only check the control-plane building if he's actually *standing inside it*. If Kubernetes drops his visit (the Job) onto a worker node by accident, he walks in, finds no manifests at all, and reports nothing useful — like sending an inspector to the wrong address.

So you **pin his visit to the control-plane node**. Two things do that together:

- a **`nodeSelector`** that says "only the node wearing the `control-plane` label,"
- and a **toleration** for the control-plane's "keep out" sign (the `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule` taint), because control-plane nodes normally refuse ordinary pods.

Then you run `--targets master` so he reads the section-1 checklist, and you read his report from the logs — now you'll see lines like `[PASS] 1.1.1` or `[FAIL] 1.2.x`.

**Watch out for:**

- **Wrong node = empty report.** Without the nodeSelector + toleration the Job can land on a worker, where the control-plane files don't exist, so no `1.x` findings appear.
- **You need BOTH the selector and the toleration.** The selector *attracts* it to the control-plane node; the toleration *lets it past* the control-plane taint. One without the other leaves the pod `Pending`.
- **Use `--targets master`, not `node`** — that's what unlocks the section-1 control-plane checks.
- Same host mounts as before (especially `/etc/kubernetes`) so it can read the real manifests and PKI.
questions.deepDive:
## Auditing the control plane (`--targets master`) — full rundown

### Mental model
The CIS Benchmark splits controls by component. **Section 1** covers the control plane — kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, etcd, and their static manifests/PKI under `/etc/kubernetes`. kube-bench can only evaluate these when it runs **on a node that actually hosts those files** — i.e. a control-plane node. So the job isn't just "add `--targets master`"; it's "add `--targets master` **and force the pod onto the control-plane node**."

### Why the pod must land on the control plane
A worker node has no `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml`, no `etcd` manifest, no apiserver PKI. If a `--targets master` Job lands there, kube-bench finds nothing to check and emits no section-1 results. Two mechanisms pin it:

| Mechanism | Role | Why needed |
|---|---|---|
| `nodeSelector: {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: ""}` | **attracts** the pod to the CP node | selects the node carrying the control-plane label |
| Toleration for `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule` | **permits** the CP node's taint | control-plane nodes are tainted to repel normal pods |

A `nodeSelector` alone leaves the pod `Pending` (untolerated taint); a toleration alone doesn't *send* it there. You need both.

### The Job manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: kube-bench-master
  namespace: cks-bench
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector:
        node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: ""
      tolerations:
      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: kube-bench
        image: aquasec/kube-bench:latest
        command: ["kube-bench"]
        args: ["run","--targets","master"]
        volumeMounts:
        - { name: var-lib-kubelet, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet, readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-kubernetes,  mountPath: /etc/kubernetes,  readOnly: true }
        - { name: etc-systemd,     mountPath: /etc/systemd,     readOnly: true }
      volumes:
      - { name: var-lib-kubelet, hostPath: { path: /var/lib/kubelet } }
      - { name: etc-kubernetes,  hostPath: { path: /etc/kubernetes } }
      - { name: etc-systemd,     hostPath: { path: /etc/systemd } }
```

> The control-plane taint uses key `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane` and effect `NoSchedule`. `operator: Exists` (no value) is the clean way to tolerate it.

### What section 1 covers
| CIS range | Area | Typical checks |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1.x | Manifest & PKI **file perms** | `0600`/`0644`, owner `root:root` |
| 1.2.x | kube-apiserver flags | `--anonymous-auth=false`, `NodeRestriction`, `--profiling=false`, audit flags |
| 1.3.x | kube-controller-manager flags | `--use-service-account-credentials`, `--profiling=false` |
| 1.4.x | kube-scheduler flags | `--profiling=false`, bind address |

### Run and read
```bash
kubectl apply -f kube-bench-master-job.yaml
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench-master --timeout=120s
# confirm it ran ON the control-plane node:
kubectl -n cks-bench get pods -l job-name=kube-bench-master -o wide
# section-1 (master) findings:
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench-master | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL|WARN)\] 1\.'
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Missing toleration → `Pending`.** `kubectl describe pod` shows *"untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane}"*. Add the toleration.
- **Missing nodeSelector → it may land on a worker → zero section-1 results.** Always confirm with `-o wide` that it ran on the CP node.
- **Using `--targets node` here** gives section 4, not section 1 — wrong answer for a "master findings" goal.
- **Label value is empty string** (`""`), not `"true"` — the control-plane role label has no value.
- **`/etc/kubernetes` mount is essential** for section-1 file-perm checks (manifests + PKI).
- Multi-control-plane clusters: the selector lands it on *some* CP node; that's fine for the benchmark.

### Quick reference
```bash
# pin to control plane + scan master
#   nodeSelector: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: ""
#   toleration:   key=node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane Exists NoSchedule
#   args:         ["run","--targets","master"]
kubectl -n cks-bench wait --for=condition=complete job/kube-bench-master --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cks-bench logs job/kube-bench-master | grep -E '\[(PASS|FAIL)\] 1\.'
```
